body:
﻿## Source investigation (read-only, current main)

Two separate defects answer the report's question. Neither is the gate's machine-frame math.

### 1. The sim playback draws the tool rotating about its own tip - display-only

The playback timeline carries only a tool tip and a tool-axis vector (`crates/sim/src/sim.rs:188-218`, `:602-632` - a radial pose is stored as an A letter, never a work transform). The renderer poses the whole tool about the tip with a shortest-rotation map (`crates/app/src/tool_body_view.rs:151-177`: `tip + R(+Z->axis) * local`), and the part is drawn from its own document transform - no rotary transform anywhere (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/world.rs:313-348`). Across an A index the drawn tool visibly sweeps from radial to pointing down, taking the housing below Z0, while the work stays put. This is exactly what the reporter saw. This path never feeds the post gate.

### 2. The post refusal comes from the path-frame fallback, not the machine-frame law

The gate has two branches (`crates/sim/src/verify/workholding.rs:130-132`): with a resolved rotary axis it judges fixed steel in the MACHINE frame, standing the posed tool up about the rotary axis line through the WCS origin (`crates/sim/src/verify/posed_steel.rs:306-344`, `upright_turn` + `turn_about` - correct rotary-line kinematics). With NO resolved axis it falls back to judging every box in the PART frame (`frame = None`), where the posed housing band centres stay at `tip + axis*offset` (`posed_steel.rs:176-209`).

In this repro's path frame the housing band bottom is ~5 mm above Z0 but its 75 mm radius reaches ~69 mm below Z0 - into the table box (`fixture.rs:141-144`, table z from `Z.min - MAX` to 0). In the machine frame the same band stands upright at z ~93-343 mm - clear. So a phantom strike is exactly what the path-frame fallback produces for this geometry.

For the repro the machine's A line (`[1,0,0]`, turns_part, G54 at origin) should resolve, so the open question is why the fallback ran at all: check `fixture::rotary_axis_of` for this op (`fixture.rs:264-305`), and whether the held warning is a CACHED generation-time path-frame warning (`posting.rs:1326-1331`) rather than a live gate finding (`posting.rs:1100`) - generation runs the same path-frame law (`generate.rs:4568-4585`, `laws.rs:184-258` at :198). If the cached warning is what holds the post, the defect is a stale path-frame warning surviving an axis that resolves at post time.

## Findings

1. Display: the sim playback needs the rotary axis line so indexed poses draw the work turning about it (or at least the tool upright), not the tool swinging about its tip.
2. Gate: the path-frame fallback turns the housing into a 75 mm-radius club reaching ~69 mm below Z0 - with a fixed table in the judged set, any radial pose near the part refuses. The fallback should refuse by name ("cannot judge - no rotary axis resolved") rather than produce phantom strikes, and/or the cached-warning path must re-judge when the axis resolves.
3. Message: the warning names no box ("a fixture"), which made a machine-table strike read as a user-fixture bug.

Suggested split: 1 and 2 are the defects; 3 is a one-line wording fix that rides either PR.

﻿## Probe result (headless run of the repro project)

Stating the op's own axis (`stated_axis: [1, 0, 0]`) does NOT clear the refusal - the strikes at moves 3 and 99 persist on a fresh generation. So the path-frame fallback is not the (only) cause: with the axis stated, the machine-frame branch runs and still convicts.

Prime suspect, from the sweep's own math (`posed_steel.rs`): the machine-frame verdict grows the capsule radius by `rho * dth` - the most the rotary turns off the stood-up angle within the interval, floored by the proven swing. With the A-86.250 deg index proven for the WCS and the spindle housing standing far off the A line, `rho * dth` grows the 75 mm-radius housing by hundreds of mm, and the grown capsule reaches the machine table box. The refusal is then conservative-real: the model believes the housing sweeps into the table during the index, and the message gives the user nothing to distinguish that from a phantom strike.

Caveat: the probe ran the SAVED project, which predates the reporter's nose_to_axis entry (the refusal still reads "states no nose_to_axis"). The reporter's live state may differ; the saved repro is available.

## What a fix must decide

1. Whether the index swing belongs inside a CUT move's capsule growth at all, or only at the retract/index poses the index-swing clause already judges.
2. The verdict message must name the struck box and the growth terms (the pose, the swing it grew by), so a user can tell a real sweep from a phantom one.
